subject.title: Suppress model fallback notices in rooms

question: Should fallback transition banners remain user-visible in direct chats while being suppressed in group/channel rooms, or should external-channel visibility use a broader default-off or configurable policy?
rationale: The original feature intentionally made fallback transitions visible, while the canonical issue asks to prevent internal routing details from reaching external recipients; source type alone does not establish which direct chats are trusted.

options.title: Suppress only shared rooms
options.body: Keep the PR’s direct-chat behavior, but preserve lifecycle events and document that one-to-one chats continue receiving notices.

options.title: Default external notices off
options.body: Keep lifecycle events and internal diagnostics while suppressing fallback banners on external messaging channels unless an explicit supported visibility policy enables them.

options.title: Retain current behavior
options.body: Do not merge the suppression change and instead treat fallback banners as intentional verbose diagnostics across chat types.

recommendation.title: Default external notices off
recommendation.body: Keep lifecycle events and internal diagnostics while suppressing fallback banners on external messaging channels unless an explicit supported visibility policy enables them.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the combined notice, lifecycle, state, status, and WebUI behavior whose permanent visibility boundary is now being reconsidered.
